Surah 114: Al-Nas

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾. He mentioned that He is the Lord of mankind, although He is the Lord of all creation, for two reasons:

The first: because mankind are held in high regard, so by mentioning them He informs us that He is their Lord, even though they are exalted.

The second: because He commanded seeking refuge from their evil, so by mentioning them He informs us that it is He who grants refuge from them.

﴿The King of mankind, the God of mankind﴾: because among mankind there are kings, so He mentioned that He is their King; and among mankind there are those who worship other than Him, so He mentioned that He is their God and the One they worship.

﴿From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws﴾. Al-Khannas (the one who withdraws) is Satan, and regarding his being named thus there are two views:

The first: because he is much given to hiding, and from this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede﴾, meaning the stars, because they disappear after appearing.

The second: because he withdraws from the remembrance of Allah, and khanas means to retreat. The rajaz poet said:

"A companion who wavers in wavering, who increases in withdrawing from his withdrawal."

(p-379)

As for al-waswas (the whisperer) here, there are two views:

The first: that it is Satan, because he whispers to the human being. Ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿the whisperer who withdraws﴾ that he said: Satan squats upon the heart of the son of Adam; when he is heedless and forgetful, he whispers, and when he remembers Allah, the Exalted, he withdraws. According to this, there are two interpretations of al-khannas:

The first: the one who returns with whispering to desire.

The second: the one who goes out with whispering against certainty.

The second view: that it is the human's own whispering from his soul, which is the whispering by which he speaks to himself.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has overlooked for my nation what their souls whisper to them, as long as they do not act upon it or speak it."

﴿Who whispers in the breasts of mankind﴾. The whispering of Satan is the summoning to obedience to him through what reaches the heart of an imagined speech, or what falls upon the soul of a supposed matter. From this comes "al-musawwas" (one who is overcome by whispering) when whispering prevails over him, because of the joy that overtakes him. Its root is a hidden sound. Al-A'sha said:

"You hear for the jewelry a whispering when she turns, like the rustle of a wind-blown reed-bed, a rustling."

﴿From among the jinn and mankind﴾. As for the whispering of the jinn, it is the whispering of Satan as we have already mentioned. As for the whispering of mankind, there are two views:

The first: that it is the human's whispering from his own soul; this was said by Ibn Jurayj.

The second: that it is the seducing of those among mankind who lead others astray.

Qatadah said: Indeed, among mankind there are devils, and among the jinn there are devils, so we seek refuge in Allah from the devils of mankind and the jinn.(p-380)

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge for Hasan and Husayn, saying: I place you under the protection of the perfect words of Allah from every devil and vermin, and from every envious evil eye." We seek refuge in Allah from what He granted refuge from, and we ask Him for the goodness with which He granted refuge.

May Allah grant success to us and to its reader in pondering what is in it and understanding its meanings; in Him is our success, upon Him is our reliance, and all praise belongs to Allah alone, and it is sufficient. May His blessings be upon His Messenger Muhammad, the chosen, and upon his brothers among the prophets and messengers, and upon his family and companions, the pure.
